A seat starts with one airframe on the civil register: an N-number, its last airworthiness inspection, a hangar address. A transponder squawk is a signal a ground station hears from that airframe alone. One airframe backs one seat, checked each annual.

Fifty clones need fifty airframes. A used two-seater that passes inspection runs 32,000 dollars, the annual 1,400, tie-down 220 a month, so a cohort passes 1.8 million dollars before a wheel lifts. Dusting a nectar orchard pays 6,000 a season.

A float plane leaves the same ripple at the dock whether its tank is full or empty.
